concrete_requests: Report the sensor reading range observed on the most curved track.
Report whether the robot finishes the slalom, and the completion_time if it does.
Report any dependence of steering_oscillation on the sensor forward offset.
questions: Does the signal stay in a usable range on the tightest bend, or do all five sensors saturate or drop out?
Is the sensor span (±0.04 m) too wide or too narrow for the 25 mm tape, judged by how often the sum of readings falls below 0.05?
Is the forward offset of 0.03 m giving enough lead, or does the robot oscillate about the line?
Are wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg giving stable yaw response, or do they limit turn rate?
Which geometry parameter, if changed, would most reduce rms_error or line_loss_events?

intent: Establish a symmetric five-sensor baseline with a forward-biased sensor row (y = 0.03 m) and mid-range body and drivetrain values. Use it to find out whether the sensor span and lookahead are adequate on the oval, s-bend and slalom tracks, and whether the robot is limited by speed or by tracking error. Expected result: completion on the oval with moderate line-loss risk on the slalom. Later iterations will narrow the sensor span or move it forward if the signal saturates, or widen the track and wheel_track if the robot yaws too readily.
learning: No prior evidence exists. Expect the first race to show whether the five-sensor span and forward offset are the binding constraints, and whether speed or tracking error limits the score.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integration Feedback yet, so this proposal is a balanced baseline rather than a tuned design. Five sensors at 0.02 m spacing span ±0.04 m, which covers the 25 mm tape with margin while keeping at least one sensor on the line through moderate bends. The sensors sit 0.03 m ahead of the axle so the reading leads the wheels and gives the controller time to react. Sensor size 0.012 m is about half the tape width, so a centred tape gives a clear, graded response. Weights are proportional to sensor x (left positive, right negative), so the signal is a direct lateral-offset estimate. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg and body width 0.12 m are mid-range values that keep the yaw inertia moderate and the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) ≈ 0.0425 m) comfortable. Body length 0.18 m is a neutral choice. I expect a run to complete the oval at a moderate speed. The main risks are sensor saturation on tight slalom bends and speed being too low to finish in 3 s. Both should show up in the next race telemetry.
